draft.title: Reducing emissions
card: Emissions are greenhouse gases released into the air, mostly from burning fossil fuels. There are three main ways to cut them. Each has advantages and limits.
Renewable energy

Solar, wind and hydro power make electricity without burning fossil fuels, so they release very little carbon dioxide while running. Limits: solar and wind output changes with the weather and time of day, so storage or backup power is needed.
Using less energy

Better insulation, efficient appliances and less travel by car mean less fuel is burned. It can save money and can be done now. Limit: it only cuts emissions where people change habits or buy new equipment.
Carbon capture

Carbon dioxide is caught from a power station or factory and stored, often deep underground, so it does not enter the air. It lets existing plants keep running. Limits: it is costly, it uses extra energy, and the stored gas must be kept from leaking.
draft.remember: Renewables, using less energy and carbon capture can all cut emissions, and each has limits.

a.q: Which action cuts emissions by using less energy?
opts: Fitting insulation so a home needs less heating
Building a wind farm to supply a town
Storing a factory's carbon dioxide underground
Replacing a coal station with a hydro station
a.why: Insulation means less fuel is burned for heating, so it reduces the amount of energy used. A wind farm is renewable energy, not a cut in energy use. Storing carbon dioxide underground is carbon capture.
a.clue: Which one lowers how much energy is needed?

b.q: A town in Queensland gets most of its power from a large solar farm. On some cloudy evenings the town still needs power from a gas station. Which limit of renewable energy does this show?
opts: Solar output changes with weather and time of day
Solar farms release carbon dioxide while running
Solar power cannot be stored by any method
Solar farms need carbon dioxide to be captured
b.why: The town needs gas on cloudy evenings because solar output changes with the weather and time of day, so backup or storage is needed. Solar farms release very little carbon dioxide while running, so that option is wrong.
b.clue: Think about what happens to sunlight on a cloudy evening.

a.best: Fitting insulation so a home needs less heating

b.best: Solar output changes with weather and time of day
